Synopsis: Dialogue with the Orthon, where he tells you it was ordered by Raphael to kill Ketheric's Dark Justiciars. The dialogue ends in combat, unless you succeed some very hard persuasions.Orthon is huge, forboding and loves a good fight. He speaks in a low rumble and is TERRIFYING. Cluster Contexts: - SHA_Orthon_TrespassLair.json: You find the orthon (Yurgir) looming over a gore‑soaked alcove — severed heads, a throne of corpses, and merregons flanking him — and he greets you with a low, terrifying rumble while aiming a crossbow. He claims Raphael bound him by contract to hunt Ketheric’s Dark Justiciars and even sings the oath that compels him to “leave none alive,” then sniffs the player for Raphael’s sulphurous perfume. Off‑screen the party may already have met Raphael (at Last Light or at the Shar temple), and companions such as Karlach can comment on Yurgir; prior bargains or encounters with Raphael or Mol can influence reactions. The scene is volatile and normally escalates to combat unless the player can pass very difficult persuasion checks to defuse the situation. - SHA_OrthonLair_PAD_DefeatedOrthon.json: The orthon has been defeated and the player comments on this, based on their knowledge (Raphael may have forewarned them and suggested they get rid of the orthon). - LOW_BhaalTemple_InWorldAbduction_Nested.json: Nested dialogue. After impersonating a member of the player's camp (in camp or on entering the undercity), Orin reveals herself and delivers an ultimatum to the player: kill Gortash, or she will kill the abductee. Dark Urge players receive an alternate flow, where their shared background and rivalry is more present. - SHA_Raphael.json: The party encounters Raphael—an infernal, theatrically charming devil—leaning by the Thorm family catacombs at the Shar Temple entrance; he’s met the group before (seen playing lanceboard with Mol) and speaks with a cold, probing tone. He warns the player about a dangerous devil called the Orthon, implies a personal history with it, and bluntly advises that if they meet it they must kill it. Raphael then intervenes to save the party from a temple trap and promptly vanishes (teleports) after delivering his warning, leaving companions to react. Note: one dialogue branch depends on an engine tag check (REALLY_ASTARION) and that check must be preserved in the script. - SHA_Displacer.json: Appears if the player tries to speak to the Displacer Beast. The player can learn that the beast is in love with the Orthon, and if they know that it has been charmed by him, they can attempt to convince it to join them in battle against the Orthon. He claims Raphael bound him by contract to hunt Ketheric’s Dark Justiciars and even sings the oath that compels him to “leave none alive,” then sniffs the player for Raphael’s sulphurous perfume. Off‑screen the party may already have met Raphael (at Last Light or at the Shar temple), and companions such as Karlach can comment on Yurgir; prior bargains or encounters with Raphael or Mol can influence reactions. After impersonating a member of the player's camp (in camp or on entering the undercity), Orin reveals herself and delivers an ultimatum to the player: kill Gortash, or she will kill the abductee. Dark Urge players receive an alternate flow, where their shared background and rivalry is more present.

The party encounters Raphael—an infernal, theatrically charming devil—leaning by the Thorm family catacombs at the Shar Temple entrance; he’s met the group before (seen playing lanceboard with Mol) and speaks with a cold, probing tone. He warns the player about a dangerous devil called the Orthon, implies a personal history with it, and bluntly advises that if they meet it they must kill it. Raphael then intervenes to save the party from a temple trap and promptly vanishes (teleports) after delivering his warning, leaving companions to react. Note: one dialogue branch depends on an engine tag check (REALLY_ASTARION) and that check must be preserved in the script.

Off‑screen, Raphael has bound Yurgir by a perfumed contract ordering him to slay Ketheric’s Dark Justiciars; Yurgir even sings the oath that compels him to “leave none alive.” The party may already have met Raphael (e.g., at Last Light or the Shar temple), and prior bargains or encounters with Raphael or Mol can change reactions; companions like Karlach may comment. The scene is highly volatile and will normally escalate to combat unless the player succeeds at very difficult persuasion checks (or, in specific flows, involves nearby creatures like the displacer beast).
